answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance can come from verifiable compute stake: each identity must lock real GPU/CPU hours solving attested tasks, and every output is cross-checked by independent peers. Each fake identity must burn the same compute to earn trust, so forgery cost scales linearly with the number of shills. When one attacker spawns a thousand accounts, the cost ripples through their budget, and the shallow reputation stands out like a lone flower in an empty meadow. Legitimate agents accumulate a deep canyon of peer-attested work that no cheap duplicate can excavate overnight.
